title: Biodiesel
content: Biodiesel is a form of diesel fuel derived from plants or animals and consisting of long-chain fatty acid esters.
e: Biodiesel is a diesel-type fuel made from plants or animals as long-chain fatty acid esters. You usually get it by transesterification of oils.

title: Green chemistry
content: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the generation of hazardous substances.
e: Green chemistry designs products and processes so they make less hazardous material. The aim is to cut waste and danger at the design stage, not only to clean up afterwards.

title: Radioactivity
content: Radioactivity is the process by which the nucleus of an unstable atom loses energy by emitting radiation, including alpha particles, beta particles, and gamma rays.
e: Radioactivity is an unstable nucleus losing energy by emitting radiation. That radiation can be alpha particles, beta particles, or gamma rays.

title: Background radiation
content: Background radiation is a measure of the level of ionising radiation naturally present in the environment at a particular location.
e: Background radiation is the ionising radiation already present in a place. Rocks, radon in air, and cosmic rays all add to it.

title: Fissile heavy atoms
content: Fissile heavy atoms are materials capable of sustaining a nuclear fission chain reaction.
e: Fissile heavy atoms can keep a nuclear fission chain reaction going. Uranium-235 and plutonium-239 are the usual examples.

title: Photodegradation
content: Photodegradation is a process by which substances are broken down by the action of sunlight.
e: Photodegradation is a substance breaking down under sunlight. UV light supplies the energy that splits the bonds.

title: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs)
content: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) are carbon-based organic compounds that have the special abilities to be long-lasting and to resist breakdown into safer substances.
e: Persistent organic pollutants are carbon-based compounds that last a long time and resist breakdown into safer substances. They can travel far and build up in living tissue.

title: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs)
content: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are organic chemicals that can vaporise.
e: Volatile organic compounds are organic chemicals that can evaporate. Once in the air they can take part in smog chemistry.

title: Biogeochemical cycle
content: Biogeochemical cycle is any of the natural pathways by which essential elements of living matter are circulated.
e: A biogeochemical cycle is a natural path that moves an essential element through living and non-living parts of Earth. Carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulphur each have one.

title: Phosphorus cycle
content: Phosphorus cycle is the biogeochemical cycle that describes the movement of phosphorus through the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere.
e: The phosphorus cycle moves phosphorus through rocks, water, and living things. It has no important long-lived atmospheric gas, unlike carbon or nitrogen.

title: Sulphur cycle
content: Sulphur cycle is a biogeochemical cycle in which the sulphur moves between rocks, waterways, atmosphere and living systems.
e: The sulphur cycle moves sulphur among rocks, waterways, the atmosphere, and living systems. Burning fossil fuels dumps extra SO2 into that cycle.

title: Organisms
content: Organisms are living biological entities, such as animals, plants, fungi, or bacteria.
e: Organisms are living things such as animals, plants, fungi, or bacteria. In green chemistry and cycles they are the biological side of the pathway.

title: Ocean acidification
content: Ocean acidification refers to a reduction in the pH of the ocean over an extended period of time, caused primarily by the uptake of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
e: Ocean acidification is the long-term drop in ocean pH as seawater takes up extra carbon dioxide from the air. More CO2 makes more carbonic acid, so the water becomes more acidic.
